  "candidates": [
    {
      "startEvent": 105,
      "endEvent": 115,
      "contextStartEvent": 84,
      "contextEndEvent": 143,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "that's irrelevant to the question at hand tonight is there a god",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Shermer expressly excludes resurrection evidence from the existence question (E105–115). Distinguishing a generic creator from Christianity supplies a reason for separating questions, but does not establish that evidence for a particular divine intervention is irrelevant to either. This is an exclusion protecting the inquiry's boundary, not a compact slogan; Lennox challenges it at E791–798."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 510,
      "endEvent": 519,
      "contextStartEvent": 493,
      "contextEndEvent": 521,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "you can only find a super powerful intelligent being",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The alien-technology example supplies a real underdetermination argument: impressive powers need not establish divinity (E493–514). The categorical claim that reasoning can never find a deity extends beyond that example without explaining why distinguishing evidence is impossible. It is unclear whether this closes off every possible result or summarizes the narrower identification difficulty."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 925,
      "endEvent": 928,
      "contextStartEvent": 731,
      "contextEndEvent": 955,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "you simultaneously remove all hope",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort", "fear"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Taken literally, removing God removes 'all hope' without a reason excluding ordinary human hopes. However, E752–770 specifically concern final justice for otherwise unredressed suffering, which substantially narrows the intended claim. E929–941 acknowledge unresolved suffering and condition the Christian response on the resurrection; there is no explicit neutralization of objections."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1593,
      "endEvent": 1599,
      "contextStartEvent": 1563,
      "contextEndEvent": 1618,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "the new atheists believe it is an illusion and therefore they have no grounds for morality",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Lennox uses this conclusion to redirect a question about why justice should exist toward morality's foundation (E1593–1603). Earlier quotations and his determinism argument supply reasons (E705–730), but the extension to the new atheists collectively remains unearned. He explicitly respects atheist conduct; rejecting an account of moral grounding does not itself immunize his position."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1608,
      "endEvent": 1615,
      "contextStartEvent": 1576,
      "contextEndEvent": 1624,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "simply say we have forgotten God",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["fear", "identity"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "Lennox adopts Solzhenitsyn's compressed explanation of mass deaths as support against the social/evolutionary morality account (E1604–1615). Neither the quotation nor his preceding moral-grounding argument establishes the historical causal link between forgetting God and those deaths. Shermer supplies a Christian-war counterexample at E1619–1624; Lennox does not explicitly render such counterexamples inadmissible."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1757,
      "endEvent": 1761,
      "contextStartEvent": 1733,
      "contextEndEvent": 1783,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "it was Christianity that freed the slaves",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "The paired claims credit Christianity with emancipation and secularism with restoring slavery, presenting a settled historical allocation without the needed causal history (E1757–1761). Earlier examples of Christian care and equal worth offer a possible motivation, not that allocation. Lennox acknowledges atheist caregivers at E1755–1756; Shermer directly contests the slavery claim at E1763–1783."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2085,
      "endEvent": 2103,
      "contextStartEvent": 2073,
      "contextEndEvent": 2112,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "unless you give up your skepticism",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Making commitment necessary for knowing the relationship could discourage continued criticism (E2094–2103). However, Lennox analogizes acquaintance and marriage, endorses initial checking, and expressly bases commitment on accumulated evidence (E2075–2084, E2101–2108). The text does not establish that subsequent objections must be rejected or that unsuccessful commitment confirms Christianity."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2130,
      "endEvent": 2136,
      "contextStartEvent": 2125,
      "contextEndEvent": 2145,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "militant agnostic I don't know and you don't either",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["ridicule"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Shermer endorses the bumper sticker and extends its denial of knowledge to Lennox and everyone (E2130–2136). That extension lacks a distinct argument establishing others' ignorance. Nevertheless, he immediately limits the examples to suffering and pre-Big-Bang questions, both discussed as difficult or unresolved, and welcomes future discovery (E2137–2145)."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 1387,
      "endEvent": 1402,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "it doesn't determine truth",
      "explanation": "Lennox accepts Shermer's distinction between psychological comfort and truth, applies it symmetrically to atheism, and redirects attention to evidence. This also qualifies how his earlier personal account of religious hope should be interpreted."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 312,
      "endEvent": 324,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "we have to collect more data and test",
      "explanation": "Shermer explicitly labels the proposed universe-selection explanation theoretical and calls for further testing. His subsequent 'I don't know' summarizes acknowledged uncertainty after an explanatory proposal; it does not replace a missing proof with an affirmation."
    }
  ]
